An Italian firm is trying a week with no internal emails in an effort to reduce worker stress. Workers are asked to talk to co workers instead as long as they work in the same building.

Would this be a relief for you or a major problem?
Do Emails at work cause stress?

Problem. Email is, in my opinion, the best way to interact with someone if you don't need to interrupt them.

More important? Call.

Even more important? then bug them in person.

Small issues are best left to email. I do like having a log of the conversation as well since I can be forgetful. But if the discussion has any amount of emotion in it, it's probably better to handle that in person.
I'd rather interact via email than phone. Email doesn't stress me. Phones ringing do

I love email and the easy paper trail they create so without them I would be extremely stressed. Email also makes it super easy for me to conduct business when I want instead of having to answer/ask questions when my schedule aligns with another persons schedule.

My problem is sifting through the quantity of emails. I have so many emails that say "If you are due for X training, there will be training at X." Well, that's probably 5 people out of several hundred. Plenty more emails that don't apply to me that I can't block.

The only time email stresses me out at work is when I DON'T receive them. Waiting on someone else to do your job is the worst. I actually enjoy my job so I hate wasting time on the clock. Our culture is pretty direct though so internal emails are mostly just followups to things we talk to other people in the office about. We are all on the same floor so if someone needs something they usually just come ask for it and you send what they need through an email.
